package_policy: No langgraph package may be installed or vendored. Quotes are published-source excerpts only.

quotes.quote: Inspired by Google's Pregel system, the program proceeds in discrete "super-steps." A super-step can be considered a single iteration over the graph nodes. Nodes that run in parallel are part of the same super-step, while nodes that run sequentially belong to separate super-steps.
If no reducer function is explicitly specified then it is assumed that all updates to that key should override it.
Every reducer is a binary function with two positional arguments: Left argument: The current value already stored in state for that key. Right argument: The update for that key returned by a node.

we've used the Annotated type to specify a reducer function (operator.add) for the second key (bar). ... If the second node returns {"bar": ["bye"]} then the State would then be {"foo": 2, "bar": ["hi", "bye"]}
If provided, this Checkpointer serves as a fully versioned "short-term memory" for the graph, allowing it to be paused, resumed, and replayed from any point.
The thread_id is the key used to store and retrieve checkpoints. Use a unique ID for independent runs, or reuse the same ID to accumulate state across invocations
interrupt_before: An optional list of node names to interrupt before.
The node restarts from the beginning of the node where the interrupt() was called when resumed, so any code before the interrupt runs again
Add a conditional edge from the starting node to any number of destination nodes. path_map: Optional mapping of paths to node names. If omitted the paths returned by the path should be node names.
you can use the prebuilt add_messages function. For brand new messages, it will simply append to existing list, but it will also handle the updates for existing messages correctly.
